newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Renault's Brazil unit drops distributor.
newsitem.headline: Renault's Brazil unit drops distributor.

text.p: French carmaker Renault SA Brazilian unit said it has terminated its contract with local car distributor CAOA because it alleged the firm was not doing a good enough job.
"We broke up with CAOA group because the company was not providing clients with satisfactory service," said a spokeswoman at Renault Comercial do Brasil SA, the company's local sales unit.
CAOA group sold Renault cars in the cities of Sao Paulo, Santo Andre, Campinas and Guarulhos, which account for 54.5 percent of Renault's market in Brazil.
Renault has 33,000 auto-service clients in Brazil, she said.
CAOA group had 12 Renault shops in Sao Paulo state. In other states, Renault cars are sold in agreement with business groups, she added.
Renault hopes to find a new distributor for Sao Paulo in the next couple of weeks, she added.
Renault's first car plant in Brazil is expected to start operating on late 1998 in the southern state of Parana, where it will produce medium-sized Megane cars, she said.
